item.title: Amish Fall Farmhouse Experience at Old Windmill Farm — Fri Sep 25 — Old Windmill Farm
item.description:
An autumn afternoon in our farm kitchen. Join us as we bake bread, churn butter from our own cows’ cream, and press apple cider with a traditional hand-cranked apple press. Then sit down and enjoy all three together, with the freshly churned butter on the bread warm from the oven.
Press fresh cider with a traditional press Churn butter from our own cows’ cream Enjoy freshly baked bread Drink cider and eat bread with fresh butter A working farm kitchen, not a demonstration Advance reservations required

item.description:

You’ll see rolling farmlands, pass by horse and buggies, and enjoy some of the best Ice Cream in Lancaster County! It’s a stark contrast to the usual fast-paced and congested areas of larger cities. For those craving something different or one of the best romantic date night ideas, join us! We designed this tour to be an experience you can share with someone. item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Sep 30, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: We the People First Friday — Fri Oct 2, 5:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Make the Ware Center for the Arts part of your Lancaster City First Friday route! Join us for an evening of poetry and art focused on peace, justice, and unity.
At 7 pm in Steinman Hall, join us for a free performance by Voices of Peace, a collective of five artists and activists from diverse backgrounds who use poetry to promote peace, justice, and unity. Through a curated selection of global poems, they highlight the impacts of war while emphasizing hope, resilience, and solidarity.
From 5 to 8 pm in the atrium, the 8th Annual Peace Kids to the Rescue Art Show and Silent Auction, which features artwork donated by over 70 children from ages 3 to 18, giving young artists an opportunity to use their creativity to make a difference in their communities. Proceeds from the art show and auction benefit Church World Service and the Arch Street Center.

item.title: Drink More Art: Live Painting with Sarah Hawkins at Vine Bar — Fri Oct 2, 6:00 PM — Vine Bar
item.description:
Vine Bar presents “Drink More Art,” a special First Friday collaboration featuring a live painting session by Lancaster abstract expressionist artist Sarah Hawkins.

The event will take place in the alleyway beside Endo Café, with Vine Bar’s interior enoteca serving as the alternate location in the event of inclement weather. Open to the public and held rain or shine.

item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Sep 29, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
